messages:
rachel: follow-up on the quota/abuse RFC: proposing a "probe guardrail" gateway that sits in-region to absorb noisy probes and enforce short-lived safety checks. goal: reduce bank churn and provide quick local rejects for obvious abuse.

mike: love the name. quick note: this should be strictly advisory for the bank, not a separate source of truth for fairness. gateway can refuse obviously abusive traffic but long-lived fairness must stay central.

rachel: agreed. my thought: two decision layers: 1) instant guardrail (local heuristics, blocklist, rate caps) and 2) probe coalescer + adaptive soft-allow (short TTL leases). both are ephemeral.

anjali: can you define "obviously abusive"? we need deterministic rules so we don't accidentally block legit PLG traffic.

rachel: examples: repeated identical request hashes at extreme qps, known compromised API keys, and high abuse-score deltas from the abuse stream. those map to an immediate soft-deny and an audit event.

lucas: interface sketch: Gateway.Check(tenant, route, short_hash) -> {decision: allow|soft-allow|deny, ttl_ms, probe_id, reason}. bank still authoritative for any lease_id longer than TTL. use gRPC + mTLS.

ops-bot: reminder: include privacy review if events include user payloads (INFRA-PRIV-46).

mike: how will we keep metrics useful? gateway should emit per-tenant hit/miss, rejected-by-rule, coalesced-probes, and bank-saved QPS. need these to justify the cost.

rachel: yes. plus we'll emit a reconciliation stream: gateway periodically sends sampled admits and denials to the bank for offline audit and model training. this helps catch misclassifications.

anjali: failure model: if gateway loses bank connectivity do we fail open, closed, or degrade?
achel: degrade: gateway can serve cached soft-allows up to a dynamic grace window. once grace expires, gateway returns 429s and signals edge to fall back to direct bank with stricter limits. grace window should be adaptive: shorter if bank errors are high.

lucas: adaptive TTL sounds neat but could be dangerous. we need a stable policy for oscillation avoidance. propose hysteresis: scale grace by bank p95 latency and keep a cooldown period between mode flips.

mike: agree. also add an emergency "global-throttle" flag the bank can push to gateways to force immediate strict mode. used only in true overload events.

sara: security question: how do we prevent clients from forging gateway headers? must have signed decision headers.
achel: gateway will attach X-Quota-Gateway-Sig + X-Quota-Gateway-Trace. signatures are HMAC(region_key, probe_id+decision+ttl). bank verifies on any contested admits. keys rotated via KMS.

anjali: can private/dedicated customers opt out? some will not want extra hop in their VPC.achel: yes opt-out via config. default for hosted is enabled. add X-Quota-Gateway-Version header so bank can accept v0 (legacy) and v1 (gateway-aware) paths.

lucas: rollout plan: passive mode (proxying only, collect metrics) -> canary soft-allow internal tenants -> wider PLG -> enterprise. fallback fastpath from edge proxy if gateway responds overloaded.

mike: operational sizing: start at 3 nodes/region, LRU cache ~25k keys/node, about 60-120MB. we can adjust after sim.

rachel: I ran a quick sim on current burst traces: a 3-node gateway with 3s soft TTL and 20ms coalescing cut bank QPS by ~28% on bursty routes. sample attached in the tracker.

ops-bot: action created: INFRA-1410 "probe-guardrail-gateway: proto + PoC" assigned to lucas, sara, anjali due 2w.

anjali: monitoring/runbook: gateways must export per-node health + bank-latency p95 + reconciliation lag. add an SRE play for rapid bypass if gateways cause increased client errors.

lucas: one more: add a tiny local scoring hook so gateway can combine abuse-score + local rate to compute a reject confidence. but any confident local reject must still be recorded to the bank.

rachel: yes and we'll provide a tunable threshold per-tenant-class. default conservative.

mike: docs: include an appendix on expected failure signals (bank p95 > X, error rate > Y) and the exact hysteresis math. SRE to verify in chaos testing.

sara: I'll add a debug endpoint: /v1/debug/decision?probe_id=xyz that returns sampled trace (decision, inputs, bank-verification) for 7d. access-gated.

rachel: ok next steps: lucas proto, sara PoC binary, anjali runbook + sim validation. I'll open the RFC follow-up ticket and we can sync after PoC. thanks all. :thumbsup:
